claims.text: The alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain relative to pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
WTaTiVZr has enhanced toughness relative to pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
The proposed enhancement is primarily governed by a chemically complex, entropy-stabilized microstructure.
Chemical complexity stabilizes a fine-grained grain-boundary network in WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr develops localized grain-boundary segregation, including possible Zr or Ti enrichment.
Local grain-boundary heterogeneity reduces dislocation nucleation or mobility barriers.
The proposed microstructure facilitates dynamic grain-boundary sliding.
The proposed microstructure facilitates activation of multiple slip systems.
Enhanced grain-boundary and dislocation processes delay crack initiation and propagation.
Commercial pure tungsten has a relatively homogeneous, coarse-grained microstructure.
Pure tungsten has higher barriers to dislocation motion than WTaTiVZr.
Pure tungsten has very low fracture toughness that restricts its useful operating-temperature window.
Pure tungsten exhibits brittle transgranular and intergranular failure regimes.
Plasma-facing materials are expected to operate at temperatures of at least 1000 K for long durations.
Grain-boundary-mediated deformation processes become active at temperatures of at least 1000 K.
Extreme grain refinement or irradiation effects may overshadow the proposed chemical-complexity mechanism.
The controlled comparison should match WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten for grain size and thermal history while varying composition.
Post-test WTaTiVZr should show more active dislocation processes and evidence of grain-boundary sliding than pure tungsten.

The hypothesis would be falsified if grain-size- and thermal-history-matched WTaTiVZr shows neither a statistically significant mechanical-property improvement nor the proposed microstructural activity relative to pure tungsten.

contradictions.description: The explanation partly attributes improved behavior to a finer grain-boundary network and contrasts fine-grained WTaTiVZr with coarse-grained tungsten, but the controlled experiment requires similar grain sizes and states that composition should be the only variable. Matching grain size removes the asserted finer-grain difference rather than directly testing it.
